facts.label: UK guidance country list
facts.text: Kazakhstan is among the countries the UK guidance for businesses names for enhanced due diligence (list as updated 12 Mar 2026; the guidance says the list is not exhaustive).

facts.label: UK signal
facts.text: UK signal: UK exports over the 12 published months at least 2x the 2019-21 average and at least £20,000 above it, for 3 months running.

facts.label: Onward signal
facts.text: Onward signal: the corridor's reported exports of the code to Russia at least 2x the 2019-21 average and at least $100,000, on the latest annual figures released by the run or, where monthly figures exist, on the latest 12 released months (the same 2x and $100,000).

facts.label: Lead and watch
facts.text: A lead has the UK and onward signals both on; a watch item has the UK signal on and the onward signal off.

facts.label: Linked cases
facts.text: Linked cases: EU-01. They are enforcement cases whose goods map to this corridor and this code or its four-digit heading. The case register records no UK involvement in them: they named no UK goods or UK party.

cases.outcome: conviction and confiscation at first instance; confiscation reduced on appeal [Likely]
cases.basis: published reports only; no official judgment seen
cases.text: EU-01 (Netherlands): conviction and confiscation at first instance; confiscation reduced on appeal [Likely]. Basis: published reports only; no official judgment seen. First public action: Oct 2024 (earliest dated step found). Linked by this corridor and code.

limits.label: A lead, not a finding
limits.text: The radar flags rises in published trade figures for a person to check. A rise in exports is a lead, not evidence of a breach.

limits.label: Onward figures are corridor totals
limits.text: Onward figures are Kazakhstan's reported exports of the code to Russia from every origin, not UK goods; they cannot show where the goods came from.

limits.label: Age of the onward figures
limits.text: The annual onward figures are for 2025, released on 20 Aug 2026; that year ended 10 months before the October 2026 run. The monthly figures run to Apr 2026.

limits.label: One month can carry the total
limits.text: One large month can carry a 12-month total: the display rule needs exports in at least 6 of the 12 months, but one large consignment with smaller sales in five other months still passes.

limits.label: A broad goods code
limits.text: HS 851762 covers a broad group of goods (machines for the reception, conversion and transmission of voice, images or other data); the figures cannot say which goods within it rose, or who traded them.

limits.label: Revisions
limits.text: HMRC and UN Comtrade revise published figures; these are the figures held at this run, and later releases may change them.

limits.label: One run
limits.text: This brief is for the October 2026 run only; a series can leave the list at a later run.

limits.label: Runs drawn after the cases
limits.text: On this route, runs are drawn only when their 12 months start after the latest first public action of a linked case (Oct 2024). The case register states no end date for the conduct in EU-01, so it cannot confirm that these runs start after the period that case covers; they most likely do.

red_flags.question: Do the goods fall within the Common High Priority Items List, and what checks show that their end destination is not Russia?
red_flags.why: The FCDO's list page says businesses should undertake due diligence to ensure that the end destination of these products is not Russia.
red_flags.applies_to: Exports of goods on the Common High Priority Items List

citation.publisher: Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
citation.title: Russia Sanctions – Common High Priority Items List

red_flags.question: Is the destination, or any country the goods pass through, one that the UK guidance names for enhanced due diligence?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists transit via a country for which additional due diligence is suggested, and names countries for enhanced due diligence including Armenia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Türkiye, the UAE and Uzbekistan; it says the list is not exhaustive.
red_flags.applies_to: Shipments to or through corridor countries

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Is the customer new, and was it incorporated outside the UK after 24 February 2022 with a line of business in military or dual-use goods?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists a new customer whose line of business includes trade in military or dual-use goods and that was incorporated overseas after 24 February 2022.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Is the customer new to importing or exporting goods on the Common High Priority Items List?
red_flags.why: The G7 industry guidance lists new importers or exporters of Common High Priority List items as a red flag.

citation.publisher: G7 Sub-Working Group on Export Control Enforcement
citation.title: Preventing Russian Export Control and Sanctions Evasion: Updated Guidance for Industry

red_flags.question: Have an existing customer's orders risen in volume or value beyond its usual pattern, and is there a business reason for the rise?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists anomalous increases in the volume or value of orders placed by existing customers.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Did the customer start receiving these goods only after 24 February 2022, or receive far more of them since then?
red_flags.why: The 2023 US supplemental alert lists an existing customer that did not receive exports under the nine high priority HS codes before 24 February 2022 but receives them now, and one whose exports under those codes rose significantly after that date.

citation.publisher: US Treasury Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
citation.title: Supplemental Alert: FinCEN and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security Urge Continued Vigilance for Potential Russian Export Control Evasion Attempts (FIN-2023-Alert004)

red_flags.question: Are the goods going out in small, frequent shipments to one central location, such as a warehouse in a third country, where they are combined into one shipment?
red_flags.why: The G7 industry guidance lists, among concerning business practices, items that may arrive in small, frequent shipments to a central location, such as a warehouse in a third country, where they are combined into one shipment. It describes the practice as often used for luxury goods; applying it to these goods is our reading.

citation.publisher: G7 Sub-Working Group on Export Control Enforcement
citation.title: Preventing Russian Export Control and Sanctions Evasion: Updated Guidance for Industry

red_flags.question: Do the goods and their capabilities fit the buyer's and the end user's line of business?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists product capabilities that do not fit the buyer's or end user's line of business.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Has the customer given clear details of the end user, the intended end use and its own ownership when asked?
red_flags.why: The 2023 US supplemental alert lists a customer that lacks or refuses to provide details to banks, shippers or third parties, including about end users, intended end use or company ownership.

citation.publisher: US Treasury Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
citation.title: Supplemental Alert: FinCEN and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security Urge Continued Vigilance for Potential Russian Export Control Evasion Attempts (FIN-2023-Alert004)

red_flags.question: Who is the end user, and can an end-user certificate be provided and checked?
red_flags.why: The European Commission's guidance for EU operators asks who the end user is and whether the end-user certificate can be provided.

citation.publisher: European Commission
citation.title: Guidance for EU operators: Implementing enhanced due diligence to shield against Russia sanctions circumvention

red_flags.question: Where a civilian end use or end user is stated, does anything link the customer or other parties to military users?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists a civilian end use or end user being claimed while the customer or other parties have military connections.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Is the customer open about where the goods will end up and what they are for?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists a customer that tries by any means to obscure the product's ultimate destination and purpose.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Is the consignee a business that would use the goods, rather than a bank, a mail centre or a logistics firm?
red_flags.why: The 2023 US supplemental alert lists ultimate consignees that do not typically engage in business consistent with using the goods, such as financial institutions, mail centres or logistics companies.

citation.publisher: US Treasury Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
citation.title: Supplemental Alert: FinCEN and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security Urge Continued Vigilance for Potential Russian Export Control Evasion Attempts (FIN-2023-Alert004)

red_flags.question: Is a freight forwarder named as the final destination of the goods?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists a freight-forwarding firm being listed as the product's final destination.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Does payment come from the customer itself, or from a party in a third country that is not otherwise part of the deal?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists payments from entities located in third countries that are not otherwise involved in the transaction. The 2022 US alert lists the same where the third country is known to be a potential transshipment point for exports to Russia and Belarus.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Has the customer asked for a non-standard payment route, such as outside SWIFT, through smaller overseas banks or in cryptocurrency, or offered cash for an expensive item?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists requests for non-standard payment routes, and a customer willing to pay cash for an expensive item when the terms of sale would normally require financing.

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation
citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Is the customer paying well above the market price, or are invoices split so that each stays under a control limit?

citation.publisher: Department for Business and Trade and Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation

red_flags.question: Is the same end user's foreign bank account making smaller payments to several similar suppliers of dual-use goods?
red_flags.why: The 2023 US supplemental alert lists smaller-volume payments from the same end user's foreign bank account to multiple, similar suppliers of dual-use products.

citation.publisher: US Treasury Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and US Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)
citation.title: Supplemental Alert: FinCEN and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security Urge Continued Vigilance for Potential Russian Export Control Evasion Attempts (FIN-2023-Alert004)

red_flags.question: Under a letter of credit, are the goods consigned to the actual end user rather than to the issuing bank?
red_flags.why: The NCA red alert lists purchases under a letter of credit that are consigned to the issuing bank, not to the actual end user.

citation.publisher: National Crime Agency (National Economic Crime Centre), with HM Treasury's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation and the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
citation.title: Red Alert: Exporting High Risk Goods

red_flags.question: Has a payment that was scheduled to come from a country of concern been rerouted at the last minute?
red_flags.why: The NCA red alert lists transactions involving a last-minute change in payment routing that was previously scheduled from a country of concern.

red_flags.question: Is the shipping route clear and usual for these goods and this destination, or complex and through several third countries?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists an unclear transportation route, or a complex route involving multiple third countries.

citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Has the way these goods are shipped to this customer changed since sanctions were imposed?
red_flags.why: The European Commission's guidance for EU operators asks whether the method of transport or shipping has changed since the imposition of sanctions.

citation.publisher: European Commission
citation.title: Guidance for EU operators: Implementing enhanced due diligence to shield against Russia sanctions circumvention

red_flags.question: Are delivery dates or destinations vague, or are several third-country freight forwarders used on one transaction?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists vague delivery dates or deliveries planned for remote destinations, and the use of multiple third-country freight forwarders or shippers on a single transaction.

red_flags.question: Do the supporting documents name the actual end user, and are they complete and consistent?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists supporting documents that do not list the actual end user or are otherwise vague, and false, inaccurate or missing documentation.

citation.title: Countering Russian sanctions evasion - guidance for businesses

red_flags.question: Are the goods recorded under the correct HS code on every document?
red_flags.why: The UK guidance for businesses lists goods recorded under a false Harmonised System code that is not subject to sanctions or export controls.
